title: Attention kernel optimization profiling — FlashAttention / paged / fused ops
content:
Summary:
Quick profiling notes from the attention kernel optimization sprint (FlashAttention variants, paged attention prototype, and fused op experiments). Goal was to understand per-kernel bottlenecks across sequence lengths and batch sizes we see in production, and produce targeted optimization/rollout guidance for the runtime.

Hardware & baseline:
- Machine: p4d-like instance (8x A100-40GB) and single A100-40GB dev node for microbenchmarks
- CUDA 12.x, cuBLAS/cuDNN updated to matching versions, PyTorch 2.1+ with AMP enabled for kernels that support it
- Model families: 7B and 13B baseline weights (decoder-only) used for synthetic traces
- Baseline runtime: our optimized serving runtime (continuous batching enabled, KV cache managed in GPU memory)

What we measured:
- Wall-clock token latency (p50/p95/p99) for generation step across sequence lengths: {32, 128, 512, 1024, 2048}
- Tokens/sec (throughput) for steady-state generation at batch sizes [1,2,4,8]
- Per-kernel time and GPU metrics (SM utilization, achieved occupancy, DRAM BW, L2 hit ratio) using Nsight Systems (nsys) and Nsight Compute (ncu)
- Kernel launch counts and CPU->GPU memcpy times for KV updates (important for paged attention)

Key experiments run (commands/snippets):
- System-wide timeline + CPU/GPU activities (nsys):
  nsys profile --output attention-profile --sample=none --capture-range ctimed --trace=cuda,nvtx python serve_microbench.py --seq 512 --bs 4

- Kernel-level counters for a specific kernel (ncu):
  ncu --target-processes all --metrics sm__throughput.avg,dram__throughput.avg,sm__inst_executed.avg --set full attention_kernels_binary

- Lightweight microbench harness (torch) to measure forward step latency:
  python microbench_attention.py --model 7B --seq 512 --batch 4 --iters 200 --mode flash/paged/fused

Observations & results (high level):
1) FlashAttention (FA) vs baseline (naive matmul+softmax+matmul)
   - FA reduces peak GPU memory (no explicit large QK matrix materialization) and shows biggest win at long seqs (>512).
   - Throughput: +20-45% tokens/s for seq >= 512 depending on batch size; smaller gains or parity at seq <= 128 due to kernel-launch overhead dominating.
   - Latency: p50 improves consistently, p95 improvements are less dramatic for low-batch (bs=1) workloads because CPU-side overhead and kernel launch cost become dominant.
   - NsightCompute shows lower DRAM throughput for FA and higher L2 reuse. SM utilization improves for large seqs.

2) Paged attention (our prototype for memory-constrained KV cache)
   - Idea: keep only active KV slices in GPU memory and page others from host (or NVMe) when not needed; reduces GPU memory pressure at cost of transfer overhead.
   - Observed behavior: when page hit rate is high (working set fits mostly on GPU), overhead is small (~5-10% latency). When paging occurs frequently, p95/p99 latencies spike massively (2x-5x) because of PCIe/NVLink copy stalls.
   - Paging threshold behaved as expected: once KV size > ~70% GPU, significant copy activity appears. For long contexts (>= 2048) with bs>1, paging becomes the main bottleneck.
   - Recommendation: use paged attention only for best-effort, non-latency-critical workloads or when combined with prefetching heuristics and asynchronous copies + overlap of compute.

3) Fused ops (combine softmax + scaling + dropout + output projection into single kernel)
   - Fusing reduces kernel launches and intermediate writes, giving consistent latency wins for small-to-medium seqs (seq 32..512). Typical latency win: 10-25% p50; up to 30% on tightly tiled kernels for small batches.
   - For very large seqs, fused kernels had mixed results: sometimes reduced DRAM pressure but increased register pressure leading to slightly lower occupancy. Need more tiling experiments and register footprint tuning.

Micro numbers (representative - dev node, A100-40GB):
- 7B model, seq=128, bs=1: baseline latency p50=36ms, FA p50=31ms, fused p50=28ms
- 7B model, seq=512, bs=4: baseline throughput=420 tok/s, FA throughput=630 tok/s, fused throughput similar to FA
- 13B model, seq=1024, bs=2: baseline p95=420ms, FA p95=300ms, paged attention (without prefetch) p95=980ms (paging storms)
(These are illustrative; full datasets are in linked_artifacts S3 zip)

Profiling artifacts / hotspots we repeatedly saw:
- Many small kernel launches owned by attention wrapper: launch overhead is nontrivial for bs<=2 and seq<=128. Fusing eliminates many of these.
- CPU-side KV management logic: synchronous memcpy and blocking API usage shows up frequently as gaps on the GPU timeline. Need to use non-blocking copies and better JVM/worker thread pinning.
- Memory bandwidth limits when sequence length grows: DRAM throughput approaches device limits for naive attention; FA shifts some pressure to compute (more SM ops) but reduces DRAM.
- Shared memory / register pressure for fused kernels: some kernels exceed per-SM register budget, reducing occupancy. Tuning tile sizes matters.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Prefetching strategy for paged attention: design heuristics (lookahead in request stream) to avoid page storms. Benchmark asynchronous prefetch overlap.
- Kernel autotuner: can we collect per-model/seq/batch profiles and pick kernel version (FA vs fused vs paged) at runtime? Add to routing heuristics.
- Investigate compiler flows (nvcc vs Triton) — Triton fused kernels sometimes performed better for small seqs; need reproducible harness and CI microbench.
- Re-run on H100 (if available) — register pressure and async copy behavior may differ.

Action items / short-term recommendations:
- Roll out FlashAttention variant for seq >= 512 by default on dedicated pools. Add canary routes for production traffic to detect regressions. (Owner: Evan)
- Gate paged attention behind an opt-in flag and only enable for non-SLA customers until prefetching is implemented. (Owner: Leila)
- Add fused attention kernels for small seq low-batch workloads in the runtime, with fallback to FA for longer seqs; add autotuner that picks kernel per-request class. (Owner: Ravi)
- Improve profiling instrumentation in runtime: emit NVTX ranges per attention stage + aggregated metrics to S3 for dashboards.

Notes / scratch:
- See GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482 for Triton fused kernel prototype and microbench harness.
- Confluence page has full tables and CSV exports (CONFLUENCE-ATTN-KERNELS-2024).

Unresolved risks:
- Paged attention may be risky for enterprise customers with hard p99 SLOs unless prefetching and backpressure are rock solid.
- Autotuning kernel selection increases runtime complexity; need strong fallbacks and telemetry.

If you want, I can extract the raw nsys/ncu command outputs and the CSV of per-kernel timings into a small dashboard for the console team to consume (I already uploaded raw traces to s3).

End of notes.
